issues.failure_explanation: Expanding gamma(s) yields, for every index set S with |S|>=2, both a C-type term s^{|S|+1} C x_{k in S}[Udot_k 0] x_{k notin S}[U_k U_{k,1}] and a G-type term s^{|S|} G x_{k in S} Udot_k x U_j. For the SAME S these two terms occupy the same mode subspaces and are not orthogonal: e.g. for d=2 the remainder is s^2(Udot[C_{11} C_{12}][V V_1]^T + [U U_1]C[Vdot 0]^T + Udot G Vdot^T) + s^3 Udot C_{11} Vdot^T, and <Udot G Vdot^T, Udot C_{11} Vdot^T> = tr(G^T (Udot^T Udot) C_{11} (Vdot^T Vdot)^T) is nonzero in general (e.g. orthonormal-column Udot, Vdot and C_{11}=G). So the claimed equality of ||gamma(s)-(X+sV)||^2 with the displayed sum of squared norms (even powers of s only; the cross terms produce s^{2|S|+1} contributions) is false. The next inequality also miscounts the level-k terms: there are binom(d,k) C-type terms with |S|=k plus binom(d,k+1) G-type terms with |S|=k+1 of the same individual bound, not just binom(d,k).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-estimate ||gamma(s)-(X+sV)|| by the triangle inequality (or Cauchy-Schwarz) over the full 2^{d+1}-term expansion, including the omitted cross terms and the corrected term counts; this yields (eq: curvature) with a larger explicit constant of the same form (a d-dependent multiple of (1+sigma_min(X)^{-2})^{d/2}), and the cosmetic constant change is propagated to atilde, abar and delta.
issues.overall_effect: The specific constant c(X)=(1/sigma_min(X)^2+1)^{d/2} in (eq: curvature) is not established; the stepsize constant atilde(X,B) in prop: backtracking GRAP, which is built from c(X), and the decrease radii delta(X_under) derived from it in prop: GRAP-R decrease and used in thm: GRAP-R inherit the unjustified value.
issues.title: Curvature lemma proof: false orthogonality and miscounted expansion terms
issues.why_classification: The defective equality is repaired by a short, routine norm estimate; every downstream statement only uses the existence of such a curvature constant, so all claims, rates of decrease, and guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 the proof's lower bound for ||V_{X_r}||, and hence delta(X_under), is only as large as the smaller of the two quantities in the min, but ||V_{X_under}|| != 0 does not imply both are positive. Counterexample: d=3, I={1}, rank_tc(X_under)=(1,2,2), r=(2,2,2), and grad f(X_under)=w x u_2 x u_3 with 0 != w perp Span(U_1), u_j in Span(U_j), and u_2 x u_3 perp Span(x_{(1)}^T) (such decomposable vectors exist since dim Span(x_{(1)}^T)=1<4). Then the first term of the exact projection already captures all of grad f(X_under), so ||V_{X_under}||=||grad f(X_under)||>0 (X_under is non-stationary), while (grad f(X_under))_{(k)} P_{Span(x_{(k)}^T)}=0 for k=1,2,3, making the second min-argument zero, so delta_bar(X_under)=delta(X_under)=0. Symmetrically, if the first min-argument vanishes and the second does not, nearby X_r can fall into the proof's first sub-case (first projection term nonzero but arbitrarily small), for which the derived bound is (c_I/2)*0=0. In both situations the proof produces no positive delta(X_under), so the sufficient decrease condition is unproven on exactly the mixed-rank locus M_{<=r}\(M_r cup M_{<r}) where apocalypse occurs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the defective min-based constant by one based on ||V_{X_under}|| itself: on the fixed-rank stratum M_r, the map Y -> ||P_{T_Y M_{<=r}}(-grad f(Y))|| is continuous (it is the maximum of the jointly continuous approximate-projection norms over the compact, continuously varying Stiefel constraints {U_{k,1}}), so there is epsilon_3(X_under)>0 with ||V_{X_r}||^2 >= ||V_{X_under}||^2/4 > 0 for all X_r in B[X_under,epsilon_3] cap M_r; setting delta_bar(X_under)=||V_{X_under}||^2/4 restores the final chain with delta(X_under)>0.
issues.overall_effect: prop: GRAP-R decrease is not established for non-stationary points where some modes are full rank and others deficient; the contradiction argument of thm: GRAP-R therefore has a gap for subsequences converging to such accumulation points, leaving the apocalypse-free guarantee of GRAP-R unproven as written.
issues.title: Sufficient-decrease constant delta(X_under) can be zero at non-stationary mixed-rank points (Case 3)
issues.why_classification: The proposition and theorem survive in full, but the repair requires a new, contained nontrivial continuity argument (or an equivalent corrected case analysis at X_under) in place of the defective constant construction; no global re-architecture and no loss of claims, hence more than a minor local fix but not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The smallest non-zero singular value of $\matx$ is denoted by $\sigma_{\min}(\matx)=\sigma_{\rank(\matx)}(\matx)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At X^{(t)}=0 every unfolding has rank 0, so sigma_min(x^{(t)}_{(k)}) = sigma_0 is undefined (there is no nonzero singular value), making the branch condition meaningless; if the branch is taken, I_k={rank-1, rank}={-1,0} contains the invalid rank -1, and the HOSVD candidate P^HO_{r_breve} with r_breve_k=-1 is undefined. The procedure therefore has no well-defined operation at the zero iterate, which the theory explicitly allows (e.g. the X=0 cases in prop: backtracking GRAP and in the convergence proofs). GRAP-R's index sets (eq: GRAP-R index) avoid this since rank_Delta(0)=0 gives I_k={0}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the degenerate case to (eq: rfGRAP index), e.g. set I_k={rank(x^{(t)}_{(k)})} when rank(x^{(t)}_{(k)})=0 (equivalently clamp rank-1 at 0 and define sigma_min(0) consistently).
issues.overall_effect: For zero initializations (or iterates hitting 0), the algorithm is not defined, so the guarantee of thm:added-1 formally does not cover such sequences.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R index sets are ill-defined at the zero tensor
issues.why_classification: A forced, purely local degenerate-case fix leaves the method, its analysis, and all guarantees unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it follows from~\cref{prop: rank delta} that $\rank_\Delta(\matx_{(k)})\leq\underline{r}_k\leq\rank(\matx_{(k)})$ for all $k\in I$ and $\rank(\matx_{(k)})=r_k=\underline{r}_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.
If $\underline{\matx}\neq 0$, it holds that $\underline{r}\leq \rank(\matx)$ for all $\matx\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\|\matx-\underline{\matx}\|_\frob<\sigma_{\min}(\underline{\matx})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claims r_under_k <= rank(x_{(k)}) (k in I) and rank(x_{(k)}) = r_k (k notin I) rest on the second part of prop: rank delta, which requires ||x_{(k)} - x_under_{(k)}||_F < sigma_min(x_under_{(k)}) for every k; this needs epsilon(X_under) to include a sigma_min(X_under)/(sqrt(d)+1)-type bound, which is absent (the analogous epsilon in prop: GRAP-R decrease does contain sigma_min(X_under)/(2(sqrt(d)+1))). Without it, for nonzero X_under with small sigma_min(X_under), nearby X can have rank(x_{(k)}) < r_under_k for k in I, destroying r_under <= r_breve and hence the HOSVD proximity ||X_{r_breve}-X_under|| <= (sqrt(d)+1)||X-X_under|| (lem: HOSVD inequality requires X_under in M_{<=r_breve}); or rank(x_{(k)}) < r_k for k notin I, so that r_breve_k = r_k is not in I_k and the candidate X_{r_breve} on which the whole proof relies is never generated by the algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include sigma_min(X_under)/(sqrt(d)+1) (up to a constant factor, as in prop: GRAP-R decrease) in the minimum defining epsilon(X_under), with the same X_under=0 case split used there.
issues.overall_effect: Case 2 of prop: rfGRAP does not cover points X at intermediate distances (roughly between sigma_min(X_under)/(sqrt(d)+1) and epsilon(X_under)) from a nonzero rank-deficient X_under; the sufficient decrease condition for rfGRAP-R, and with it thm:added-1, is not shown on the claimed neighborhood.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R decrease proof: epsilon(X_under) lacks the sigma_min-proximity needed by Proposition prop: rank delta
issues.why_classification: The fix is a forced, local addition of a standard proximity condition copied from the sibling proof; the method, the proposition's content, and all downstream guarantees are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider $\breve{\vecr}=(\breve{r}_1,\breve{r}_2,\dots,\breve{r}_d)$ with $\breve{r}_k=\min\{r_k-1,\rank(\matx_{(k)})\}$ for $k\in I$ and $\breve{r}_k=r_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted factor-1/2 continuity of ||P~_k(grad f(Y))|| = ||P^perp_{Span(y_{(k)})} (grad f(Y))_{(k)} P_{Span(y_{(k)}^T)}|| at X_under fails whenever the candidate has higher mode-k rank than X_under, which occurs since r_breve_k = min{r_k-1, rank(x_{(k)})} can exceed r_under_k for k in I: the extra singular subspaces of (X_{r_breve})_{(k)} have no continuous limit and can absorb exactly the relevant gradient component. Counterexample: d=2, x_under=diag(1,0,0), r=3, x=diag(1,delta_1,delta_2), so r_breve=2 and X_{r_breve}=diag(1,delta_1,0) -> x_under; with (grad f(x_under))_{21}=1 and (grad f(x_under))_{31}=(grad f(x_under))_{32}=0 one gets ||P~_1(grad f(X_{r_breve}))|| = ((grad f(X_{r_breve}))_{31}^2+(grad f(X_{r_breve}))_{32}^2)^{1/2} -> 0 while ||P~_1(grad f(x_under))||=1, so no such epsilon_3 exists for k=1. Two further constant-level errors compound the step: bound (i) uses c_I = prod_{k in I}(r_k - r_under_k)/min{n_k,n_{-k}} although (eq: inequality) applied at X_{r_breve} only provides the smaller c'_I = prod_{k in I}(r_k - r_breve_k)/min{n_k,n_{-k}}; and the final step ||V_hat_{X_under}|| >= prod_k sqrt(1/min{n_k,n_{-k}}) ||V_{X_under}|| is stronger than the established angle condition ||V_hat_{X_under}|| >= sqrt(c_I/(d+1)) ||V_{X_under}|| and is false in general (e.g. when [d]\I is a single mode with small min{n_k,n_{-k}}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the factor-1/2 continuity bound to k in [d]\I, where the rank is constant and continuity holds. For k in I no separate bound is needed: since Span(x_under_{(k)}^T) is contained in the relevant product space, the continuous bound (i) already satisfies ||grad f(X_under) x_{j in [d]\I} P_{U_j}|| >= ||P~_k(grad f(X_under))|| at X_under. Using (i) with the uniform constant prod_{k in I} 1/min{n_k,n_{-k}} (valid since r_k - r_breve_k >= 1) in place of c_I, and the angle condition ||V_hat_{X_under}|| >= omega_hat(X_under)||V_{X_under}||, one obtains ||V_{X_{r_breve}}|| >= (1/2)(prod_{k in I} 1/min{n_k,n_{-k}})^{1/2} omega_hat(X_under)||V_{X_under}|| > 0 and adjusts delta(X_under) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform positive lower bound on ||V_{X_{r_breve}}|| that drives the Armijo decrease in Case 2 is not established as written; consequently the sufficient decrease condition for rfGRAP-R at rank-deficient X_under, and hence the apocalypse-free claim of thm:added-1, lacks a valid proof as written.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R lower bound: false continuity across rank jumps and unjustified constants in Case 2
issues.why_classification: The proposition and theorem survive, but the repair requires a nontrivial contained re-derivation of the key lower bound (a new dominance observation plus corrected constants), which is more than a routine local fix; there is no change to the statements or loss of scope, so it is not serious.
